defect.evidence_quote: there might have been a Sixth Amendment violation
defect.locator_note: text/Hoffa v. United States__7760f9.txt, Sixth Amendment sections III.A-III.B; content_page.md holding
defect.problem: The core pre-attachment/no-duty-to-arrest point is supported, but the phrasing 'planting an informant raises no 6A problem pre-attachment' is too broad. Hoffa did not resolve whether the Government placed Partin and separately assumed a possible Sixth Amendment intrusion in the Test Fleet defense-counsel context.
defect.proposed_fix: Limit the holding to: the Government has no Sixth Amendment duty to arrest or charge once it has probable cause, and Partin's evidence on the separate jury-tampering offense was admissible because the statements were made outside counsel's presence, were not connected to the existing defense, and adversary proceedings on that offense had not begun.

reasons: The opinion supports the no-duty-to-arrest rule with the page-310 passage rejecting a forced choice between early arrest and Sixth Amendment attachment.
The opinion also narrows the informant issue: Partin's statements were about a separate offense and were not made in counsel's presence or in connection with the Test Fleet defense.
Because the Court expressly avoided the placement dispute, the word 'planting' should not be stated as the holding without qualification.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add 'as to the uncharged offense' and replace 'planting an informant raises no 6A problem' with 'using informant evidence did not violate the Sixth Amendment on these facts.'
